beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Mon Oct 19): conditional for beginners, best 6:45–9:30 AM. Evening outlook, so confidence is lower than a same-morning report; the morning on-site check decides. Small but long-period SW swell (model about 1.3 ft at 17 s at Waikīkī) and fresh to strong trades at today's strength (NWS: E around 20 mph; Honolulu gusted to 32 mph at 6 PM tonight). Rising tide toward the 11:26 AM high (1.8 ft). 9:30–11:30 AM conditional; from 11:30 AM not recommended.
beginner.recommendation: Plan early and stay flexible. NWS expects trades to hold at current strength through Monday; at 6 PM Sunday Honolulu was NE 18 mph gusting 32 mph, much windier than at dawn today (E about 6 mph), so a light dawn lull is possible but not assured. The south swell keeps declining and NWS has south shores dropping below seasonal average Monday (1–3 ft on exposed shores, not Canoes). The Waikīkī model has a small SW swell at 15–17 s: small at Canoes, but long-period, so watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before committing. NWS expects windward showers with some leeward spillover overnight and early morning, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side before going in; no DOH list could be read this run. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low at dawn. Your on-site read overrides this report.

News reports from Oct 16 describe brown-water and bacteria advisories on Oʻahu's North Shore; not confirmed today. This morning's partial list showed a Kauaʻi brown-water advisory at Anini Beach (Oct 13); not rechecked. Not finding an advisory does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: The DOH eha-cloud list blocks the fetch tool. NWS expects showers most numerous at night and early morning with some spilling to leeward areas, which raises runoff risk at Waikīkī.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
